Session Replay
The 8 best session replay tools
By Ethan Lapinski
Published Apr 28, 2025
Session Replay Pendo Session Replay
The right tool delivers benefits across various functions.
Updated September 17, 2026
If you want product growth, you need to understand user behavior. And to understand user behavior, you need the right session replay tool .
Because they’re like UHD security cameras for your product. Allowing your teams to see precisely how users move, click, scroll, and stumble through your product. You get rich, qualitative context that goes far beyond traditional analytics.
With the right tool for your specific needs, your product managers, UX designers, and developers can diagnose issues, optimize funnels, and enhance onboarding. In other words, they can elevate your software experience to grow your product.
In this short guide, we look at eight leading session replay tools: Pendo, FullStory, LogRocket, Amplitude, Quantum Metric, PostHog, Hotjar, and Glassbox. But first, context on how.
This is why session replay tools matter
With the right session replay software, you can deliver multifaceted benefits across various functions.
You can identify UI bottlenecks and friction : By replaying user sessions, your teams can pinpoint UI bottlenecks and rage clicks, and better understand drop-off points in key user journeys.
You can optimize conversion funnels and user journeys : You’re able to visualize user steps and identify hesitation or abandonment points, enabling teams to refine user flows and streamline conversion paths.
You can enhance product and UX development : Session replay tools provide direct user feedback, informing design iterations and validating new features, ensuring user-centric product development.
You can deliver cross-functional value (Product, UX, Dev, IT/Support) : You can align product, support, and dev teams around real user behavior. That means better product roadmapping, validated designs, and improved context for debugging.
You can address privacy and data masking considerations: With robust features like default text masking, configurable form privacy, and secure data encryption, you can ensure compliance with regulations like GDPR and CCPA, protecting PII while allowing analysis.

Let’s dive deeper into the best session replay tools
Now let’s take an in-depth look at the eight tools available to you. Starting with Pendo.
1. Pendo: Turn replay insights into in-app action
Best for: Product-led teams aiming to unify session replay, in-app guidance , and feedback for user adoption and continuous growth.
Key features: Unlimited, intelligently filtered session capture; unified product experience suite integrating replay with web/mobile usage analytics; powerful no-code tools for in-app surveys, tooltips, and onboarding flows; deep user segmentation; SOC2 compliance and secure data masking.
Pros: Find an onboarding drop-off in product analytics, watch the relevant sessions to understand the friction, then use in-app guides to help users through it. Pendo brings those steps together, giving product teams a way to act on what they learn from replay.
Considerations: The broader Pendo platform is most useful when your team needs product analytics and in-app guidance alongside recordings. If you only need to watch website sessions in isolation, compare that requirement with the scope and cost of the Pendo package.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Custom pricing based on MAU and modules. No-code focus aids faster deployment. SOC2 compliant, with secure data masking and session replay retention of 30 days by default, or 90 days with extended retention; saved clips remain available for up to one year.
Integrations: Extensive ecosystem including CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), Live Chat (Intercom, Zendesk), Product Tools (Jira, Optimizely), Data Warehouses (Segment, Snowflake), and BI (Looker, Tableau).
“With Pendo Session Replay, the support agent can get all the context they need without having to ask another question.”
—Lauren Lathrop, Senior Manager of Customer Support, Avero
Mobile Session Replay: See what users do on iOS and Android
Pendo Session Replay isn't limited to web apps. It captures visitor interactions across iOS and Android mobile apps, giving product teams full visibility into the mobile user experience alongside their web data. This is apart of the larger Pendo for mobile product that can excel your mobile apps.
Key mobile session replay capabilities include:
Native framework support : Supports React Native and Flutter, alongside supported iOS and Android frameworks.
Unified replay library : View web and mobile sessions in one place for complete cross-platform journey visibility
Mobile-specific frustration signals : Identify rage clicks in mobile sessions.
Privacy-first on mobile : The same text masking and PII protection you get on web, applied consistently to mobile sessions
Pendo mobile session replay tool showing user session recordings
2. FullStory : A behavioral analytics big beast
Best for: Enterprises needing deep UX insights and complex behavioral trend understanding, ideal for large organizations uncovering the why behind user actions.
Key features: Pixel-perfect session replays with smart event-tagging; integrated digital experience analytics (conversion funnels, journey mapping, heatmaps); AI-powered insights and anomaly detection; robust GDPR/CCPA compliance.
Pros: Delivers exceptionally rich, granular behavioral data across the entire customer journey for profound user observations. Its intuitive UI simplifies exploration, highly valued by product analysts and UX designers for identifying pain points and informing improvements.
Considerations: Users often report a “steep learning curve” for advanced features. Premium pricing, with “high pricing” and “significant price increases,” noted as potential drawbacks, especially for smaller companies.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Tiered pricing based on recorded sessions (estimated $2,000-$150,000+ annually). Implementation typically takes one month. “Private by Default” technology masks sensitive data, ensuring GDPR/CCPA compliance.
Integrations: Enterprise-grade integrations including Microsoft Teams for sharing session observations and Productboard for product feedback analysis.
3. LogRocket: Developer-centric debugging
Best for: Product teams with strong engineering involvement requiring detailed error tracking and frontend performance monitoring, tailored for diagnosing and resolving technical issues.
Key features: Session replays enriched with critical developer data (DOM, console, network logs) and granular frontend performance metrics (CPU, memory, load times); robust error tracking with direct replay correlation; “Galileo AI” for issue detection and prioritization.
Pros: Offers unparalleled technical depth for rapid bug reproduction and resolution. Delivers real-time error visibility tied to user sessions, significantly cutting debugging time. Captures full error context (user actions, network requests, application state). A free tier is available for smaller teams or initial evaluation.
Considerations: Highly technical nature can be less intuitive for non-technical users. Lacks native in-app guidance or feedback tools, creating a “context-to-action gap” for product-led growth, requiring external intervention tools. Session-based pricing can become “steep” for growing teams.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Offers Free, Team (from $99/month), Professional (from $350/month), and Enterprise (custom) plans. Generally “surprisingly fast to implement.” GDPR compliant with automatic data masking and self-hosted deployment options.
Integrations: Robust developer integrations including Error Reporting (Jira, Sentry), Observability (Datadog, New Relic), Data Warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake), and A/B Testing (Optimizely). Integrates with Pendo for metrics and session filters.
4. Amplitude : Data-driven product intelligence
Best for: Data-savvy teams prioritizing deep product analytics, seeking integrated session replay to contextualize quantitative observations; well-suited for product, growth, and digital marketing teams focused on data-driven strategy and experimentation.
Key features: Industry-leading, event-based product analytics (cohort, segmentation, funnel/retention tracking); seamless Session Replay integrating with core analytics to visualize digital analytics and link qualitative observations to product KPIs.
Includes AI-powered summaries, predictive observations, and robust A/B testing/experimentation tools.
Features privacy-first design with default text masking and customizable data retention.
Pros: Provides industry-leading analytics directly tied to real sessions, excellent for product strategy and experimentation.
Offers strong data governance and mobile replay support, integrating with many data platforms and CDPs.
Its strength lies in enriching existing quantitative analytics by providing a “contextual layer” to visualize the why behind data trends.
Considerations: Session replay is “not as standalone or visually detailed as others.” Typically involves a “more complex setup” and is generally better suited for “mature product orgs” with established data teams. Pricing for advanced features can be high.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Offers Free, Plus (from $49/month), Growth, and Enterprise (custom) plans. Initial setup can take 2-3 weeks, comprehensive 4-6 weeks. Privacy-first design with default text masking and GDPR/CCPA compliance.
Integrations: Extensive integrations with featured partners like Twilio Segment, Braze, AWS S3, and HubSpot. Connects with hundreds of other tools across CRM, data warehouses, and various SDKs.
5. Quantum Metric: Enterprise-grade continuous product design
Best for: Large organizations combining real-time user behavior with quantitative/qualitative product observations for continuous product design.
Key features: Real-time session replay with auto-capture of user frustration signals; robust journey mapping and segmentation; machine learning-based anomaly detection; root cause analysis and impact quantification; enterprise-grade data privacy and security.
Pros: Ideal for enterprise-scale digital teams, combining replay, analytics, and user sentiment in one comprehensive suite.
Provides strong benchmarking and prioritization tools, delivering real-time observations and quantifying business impact directly in business terms (e.g., revenue, CSAT).
Its focus on “Continuous Product Design” integrates real-time user behavior with observations for a continuous loop of design, monitoring, and optimization.
Considerations: “Higher complexity” may require heavier onboarding due to extensive capabilities. Pricing is tailored for mid-market to enterprise users, reflecting its advanced feature set and scalability. Quantum Metric isn’t just highly complex to set up, it also takes some expertise to manage and maintain.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Custom pricing (average annual cost ~$280,000). Average implementation time is 3 months. Automatically blocks sensitive data capture, uses pseudonymization and encryption for PII, and adheres to SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001 for GDPR/CCPA compliance.
Integrations: Strong partner network including Experimentation (Split, Optimizely), Customer Experience (ServiceNow, Salesforce Service Cloud), Voice of Customer (Qualtrics, Medallia), Data Platforms (Looker, Tealium), and Collaboration (Slack).
6. PostHog: Replay for product engineers
Best for: Product engineers connecting user behavior with bugs, releases, and experiments.
Key features: Session replay with console and network context, product analytics, feature flags, experiments, and AI-powered recording search and summaries.
Pros: Teams can investigate a bug in a recording, explore the behavior behind it, and use the broader platform to evaluate a product change. That makes PostHog useful when engineering and product measurement sit close together.
Considerations: Replay, analytics, and other products may be metered separately. Model the combined workflow you plan to use, especially if you expect recording and event volumes to grow together.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Usage-based pricing. Confirm current allowances and product-specific limits with PostHog. Configure recording rules and privacy masking during setup.
Integrations: Replay connects with PostHog’s wider product engineering tools.
See how the broader platforms compare in Pendo vs. PostHog .
7. Hotjar: See what visitors do and ask why
Best for: UX and marketing teams understanding website behavior and improving pages that aren’t converting.
Key features: Session recordings, heatmaps, and surveys.
Pros: Heatmaps help you spot where visitors click, scroll, and lose interest. Recordings let you follow individual journeys, while surveys help explain the decisions behind them. Together, they help teams investigate questions like why visitors abandon a signup page or overlook an important call to action.
Considerations: Recordings show behavior, while surveys rely on visitors choosing to respond. Use both to build context rather than treating either as a complete explanation. Check current recording and survey allowances instead of relying on older plan comparisons.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Free and paid plans are available. Configure capture and privacy settings before collecting visitor data.
Integrations: Evaluate how Hotjar will bring findings into existing team workflows.
8. Glassbox: Follow complex journeys across domains
Best for: Enterprise teams investigating customer journeys across websites and mobile apps, particularly in regulated industries.
Key features: Session replay, journey analytics, struggle and error analysis, configurable data masking, and AI-assisted session search and summaries.
Pros: A customer’s journey doesn’t always stay on one domain.
Glassbox can connect interactions across domains, for example, from a banking homepage to a separate login site, helping teams investigate the full experience instead of piecing together disconnected recordings.
Its privacy controls also make it relevant when sensitive customer data is part of the journey.
Considerations: The enterprise capabilities are most relevant when cross-domain journeys and data controls are central requirements. For a team primarily investigating simple website drop-offs, compare that broader scope with what you actually need.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Contact Glassbox for pricing. Include deployment requirements and masking configuration in the evaluation.
Integrations: Evaluate how Glassbox will connect journey findings with your existing analytics and issue-resolution workflows.
Pendo versus the competition
Different tools have different strengths. But Pendo’s ability to unify session replay, product analytics, web analytics, in-app guidance, and customer feedback in one interface sets it apart.
FullStory and LogRocket excel in narrower verticals (UX and development respectively).
Quantum Metric provides real-time behavioral observation at enterprise scale.
Pendo connects behavioral data with guide engagement, NPS feedback, and visual context, helping teams move from understanding friction to improving the experience.
Teams don’t just watch what happened, they act on it in real time.
And Pendo’s comprehensive approach does more than simplify your stack. It gives you a vital single source of truth for product experience data. That means greater operational efficiency and cross-functional alignment.
Choosing the best session replay software
The best session replay software for your product depends on your specific goals, product type, and data users. Here are three key questions to ask yourself:
Do we need mobile support?
If your product has a significant mobile presence, you’ll need robust mobile app replay and analytics.
Are we analytics- or dev-heavy?
Data science or product analytics teams might prioritize deep quantitative analysis (like Amplitude), while developer-centric teams might lean towards extensive debugging tools (like LogRocket).
What’s our budget and team structure?
Pricing varies. Significantly. So consider the total cost of ownership, including implementation, learning curve, and need for specialized personnel. Align the tool’s capabilities with the specific pain points and objectives of your product, UX, development, and support teams.
From identifying UI bottlenecks to fostering cross-functional alignment, session replay tools drive real product improvements. Because they give your product teams the critical user behavior insights that traditional analytics just can’t deliver.
And yes, there’s a number of solutions available to you. But if you’re looking to build a product-led growth strategy that values proactive guidance, comprehensive analytics, and seamless feedback loops, Pendo stands out as a top-tier choice.
Its unified platform simplifies understanding and improves the entire software experience lifecycle, empowering your product, sales, and IT teams to act decisively.
Of course, you need to get hands-on before you make a final decision. Demo the tool. Trail it. Test key features with your specific workflows. Choose the tool that makes your software smarter and fosters a more human, intuitive user experience. Because that’s where we all want to be.

Together, they help teams investigate questions like why visitors abandon a signup page or overlook an important call to action.

Considerations: Recordings show behavior, while surveys rely on visitors choosing to respond. Use both to build context rather than treating either as a complete explanation. Check current recording and survey allowances instead of relying on older plan comparisons.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Free and paid plans are available. Configure capture and privacy settings before collecting visitor data.
Integrations: Evaluate how Hotjar will bring findings into existing team workflows.
8. Glassbox: Follow complex journeys across domains
Best for: Enterprise teams investigating customer journeys across websites and mobile apps, particularly in regulated industries.
Key features: Session replay, journey analytics, struggle and error analysis, configurable data masking, and AI-assisted session search and summaries.
Pros: A customer’s journey doesn’t always stay on one domain.

Glassbox can connect interactions across domains, for example, from a banking homepage to a separate login site, helping teams investigate the full experience instead of piecing together disconnected recordings.
Its privacy controls also make it relevant when sensitive customer data is part of the journey.

Considerations: The enterprise capabilities are most relevant when cross-domain journeys and data controls are central requirements. For a team primarily investigating simple website drop-offs, compare that broader scope with what you actually need.
Pricing, implementation, and privacy: Contact Glassbox for pricing. Include deployment requirements and masking configuration in the evaluation.
Integrations: Evaluate how Glassbox will connect journey findings with your existing analytics and issue-resolution workflows.
Pendo versus the competition
Different tools have different strengths. But Pendo’s ability to unify session replay, product analytics, web analytics, in-app guidance, and customer feedback in one interface sets it apart.
FullStory and LogRocket excel in narrower verticals (UX and development respectively).
Quantum Metric provides real-time behavioral observation at enterprise scale.
Pendo connects behavioral data with guide engagement, NPS feedback, and visual context, helping teams move from understanding friction to improving the experience.
Teams don’t just watch what happened, they act on it in real time.

And Pendo’s comprehensive approach does more than simplify your stack. It gives you a vital single source of truth for product experience data. That means greater operational efficiency and cross-functional alignment.
Choosing the best session replay software
The best session replay software for your product depends on your specific goals, product type, and data users. Here are three key questions to ask yourself:
Do we need mobile support?
If your product has a significant mobile presence, you’ll need robust mobile app replay and analytics.
Are we analytics- or dev-heavy?
Data science or product analytics teams might prioritize deep quantitative analysis (like Amplitude), while developer-centric teams might lean towards extensive debugging tools (like LogRocket).
What’s our budget and team structure?

Pricing varies. Significantly. So consider the total cost of ownership, including implementation, learning curve, and need for specialized personnel. Align the tool’s capabilities with the specific pain points and objectives of your product, UX, development, and support teams.

From identifying UI bottlenecks to fostering cross-functional alignment, session replay tools drive real product improvements. Because they give your product teams the critical user behavior insights that traditional analytics just can’t deliver.

And yes, there’s a number of solutions available to you. But if you’re looking to build a product-led growth strategy that values proactive guidance, comprehensive analytics, and seamless feedback loops, Pendo stands out as a top-tier choice.
Its unified platform simplifies understanding and improves the entire software experience lifecycle, empowering your product, sales, and IT teams to act decisively.

Of course, you need to get hands-on before you make a final decision. Demo the tool. Trail it. Test key features with your specific workflows. Choose the tool that makes your software smarter and fosters a more human, intuitive user experience. Because that’s where we all want to be.
